credits.text: Phrases from the FSI Amharic Basic Course (public domain), Wikivoyage contributors "Amharic phrasebook", and Omniglot; native-speaker review pending.

activities.prompt: Hanna meets Dawit for the first time. Amharic questions change depending on whether you speak to a man or a woman.

activities.speaker: Hanna
activities.translation: What is your name? (to a man)

task.feedbackCorrect: Right: Simish is the form used to a woman.
task.feedbackIncorrect: Simih is used to a man, and Sint new? asks a price.
task.prompt: Now Dawit asks Hanna her name. Which question does he use?

activities.prompt: Say your own name aloud with Sime … new.

lessons.objective: Follow Hanna and Dawit meeting at a friend's house, then choose the right name question.
lessons.title: Hanna meets Dawit

examples: Simih man new? (What is your name? — to a man)
Simish man new? (What is your name? — to a woman)
activities.explanation: In these phrases the word for your changes with the person you speak to: simih (your name, to a man) and simish (your name, to a woman). Sime is my name.

task.feedbackIncorrect: Start with Simish (your name, to a woman).
Sime first, the name in the middle, new at the end.

lessons.objective: Notice the ending that changes for a man or a woman, then build both questions.
lessons.title: Speaking to a man or a woman

activities.speaker: Story
activities.text: Dawit's colleague is surprised to hear him greet her in Amharic. She asks:

activities.speaker: Story
activities.text: She answers quickly and he misses it:

activities.speaker: Dawit
activities.translation: What did you say? I don't understand

activities.speaker: Story
activities.text: She laughs, says it again slowly, and he thanks her before leaving:

task.prompt: How much Amharic does Dawit say he knows?

task.feedbackIncorrect: Listen again and check the transcript.

activities.translation: I know a little / What did you say? / Thank you
activities.unavailableReason: There is no genuine recording of these lines yet. Root will not stand in a synthetic or unrelated voice, so this listening step opens once a real speaker has recorded it. The story and its question above count on their own.

lessons.objective: Read about Dawit practising his Amharic, then answer a question.
lessons.title: Story: Dawit's first lesson

objective: Greet someone, ask their name the right way for a man or a woman, and say how much Amharic you know.
title: Greetings and introductions
